hook.text: KashLink sends USDC as a link. No address, no account, no gas. Live on Arc mainnet.

problem.text: Every cash-link product has the same problem.
The link is a fresh address. It holds the money, but has no gas to move it.
So you bolt on a relayer, a hot wallet, meta-transactions, and an API. Our Polygon version needed all four.
Arc makes every one of them unnecessary.

arc.text: On Arc, USDC is the gas.
The sender funds the link once: the amount, a one percent fee, and one cent per slot.
The contract drops that cent on the link's own address. And that cent is the gas for the claim.
The recipient signs one plain transaction with the key in the link. The chain just accepts it.
No relayer. No second token. No wallet to install first.

demo.text: Fund it once. Pick USDC or E-U-R-C, an amount, and who: one person, a link each, or an open drop.
One transaction funds everything: the money, the fee, and a cent of claim gas per person.
The key rides in the URL and never touches a server. Share it by chat, or hold up the QR code.

claim.text: For the recipient, the link arrives like any message. Nothing to install.
No wallet? Face ID creates a passkey wallet on the spot, and the claim goes straight into it.
One plain transaction, paid from the cent on the link. Instant finality: received a block later.

features.text: Cash links. A link each. Open drops. Notes and QR codes. Returns. Passkey wallets. E-U-R-C. And live stats.

contract.text: About 260 lines of Solidity, 39 Foundry tests, no proxy, no pause. The app never holds the money.
The only ways out of escrow are a claim with the link key, or a refund to the sender after expiry.
It's live on Arc mainnet, and keeps its own totals, so the stats page needs no backend.

outro.text: KashLink. Send USDC as a link. Share it like cash.
